corpusOverrides.note: Only 曩 needed a different corpus: the Japanese file writes the inner strokes of the 日 and 襄 bodies in a different order (three strokes over 60°, max 99°), and the simplified file already follows the dictionary except for one opening dot. selection.json records the starting corpus and the reason.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: The 曩 override removed two of the eight flagged strokes; the remaining four characters were resolved by reordering (覊, 儻) or by an authored path (曩, 甯). The endpoint assignment check added 糺, whose 糸 strokes run in the same direction and differ only in order. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 6 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: All six are short opening dots the dictionary draws vertically while the licensed corpora slant them (宄 1 at 52°, 襢 1 at 51° and 6 at 47°, 癉 1 at 56°, 螗 7 at 50°, 憝 1 at 60°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y); no glyph in this batch carries a horizontal offset.
